preconditions.description: The input integer n is the length of the array a, where 3 ≤ n ≤ 5000.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= i <= n for i in range(1, n + 1))
preconditions.description: Indices i and j in queries must be distinct integers between 1 and n (inclusive).
The array a is unknown but fixed for the entire interaction. All elements are positive integers not exceeding 10^5.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i <= 10**5 for a_i in a) and len(a) == n
postconditions.description: The output array a must have exactly n elements, each a positive integer not exceeding 10^5.

postconditions.expression: all(a_i == a_j for i, j in queries if i != j and (i, j) in queries and (j, i) in queries) and all(a_i + a_j == response for (i, j), response in query_responses)
postconditions.description: For every query (? i j) made, the response must equal the sum of the elements at indices i and j in the output array a. The program must not make contradictory queries (e.g., (i,j) and (j,i) must yield the same response).
The program must make at most n queries to deduce the array a.

postconditions.expression: all(a_i == a_j for i, j in range(1, n + 1) if (i, j) in queries or (j, i) in queries) and all(a_i + a_j == response for (i, j), response in query_responses)
postconditions.description: The output array a must be consistent with all query responses, meaning every queried pair (i,j) must satisfy a_i + a_j = response.
